small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime (fast_p ~0.23 with the LN+GELU+scale fused already). Further tuning of the LN kernel (e.g., ROWS_PER_PROG sweep, num_warps) will not close the gap — the headroom is in replacing the conv.
- If staying small, try ROWS_PER_PROG=2 with num_warps=2 since C=64 is tiny (BLOCK_C=64, one warp suffices); also consider processing multiple rows per program with a 2D tile (BLOCK_M × 64) to amortize weight/bias loads across rows.
- Cache weight/bias in registers (already done) and ensure the kernel uses channels_last memory ordering on the conv output so the LN reduction axis is contiguous — currently it is, since LN is over the last dim after view.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, D_in·H_in·W_in tile)` that loads an input voxel, multiplies by the `(OC, kD, kH, kW)` weight slice, and atomically adds into the output grid at positions `(d_in*stride - pad + kd, ...)`. Output shape: (32, 64, 32, 64, 64) ≈ 268M elements — this is the heavy op.
- Alternative: gather-style direct kernel — one program per `(N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)` that iterates over `(IC, kD, kH, kW)` and gathers the input from `((d_out + pad - kd) / stride)` when divisible. This avoids atomics and matches the GEMM-tile recipe in the skills doc. Start with BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=16, num_warps=4, num_stages=2.
- Fuse the bias add, LayerNorm (over OC=64, fits in one block), GELU, and scaling into the conv-transpose epilogue. Since LN normalizes across the OC axis which is small (64), a single program per output spatial location can hold the full channel vector in registers and apply LN+GELU+scale before storing — eliminating a second pass over the 268M-element tensor.
